title: Superficial parotidectomy
text: Superficial parotidectomy. In this film we follow the operation step by step on a three dimensional model of the right parotid region. The key to the operation is the facial nerve: finding its trunk safely, and following every branch through the gland.

title: Position and incision
text: The patient lies supine, with the head turned away. The eye and the corner of the mouth are left visible under a clear drape, so that facial movement can be seen, and long acting muscle relaxants are avoided if the nerve is to be monitored. A modified Blair incision runs in front of the ear, around the lobule, and down into a neck crease. A facelift incision is an alternative.

title: Skin flap
text: The anterior flap is raised superficial to the parotid fascia, as far forward as the anterior border of the gland. Going further forward risks the branches of the facial nerve, which leave the gland anteriorly and become more superficial.

title: Free the posterior gland
text: The great auricular nerve and the external jugular vein are found on sternocleidomastoid, and the posterior branch of the nerve is kept if possible. The tail of the gland is then separated from the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid and from the mastoid.

title: Along the ear canal
text: The gland is dissected forwards off the cartilage of the external acoustic meatus, down to the tragal pointer, and the upper border of the posterior belly of digastric is exposed.

title: Find the trunk
text: Gentle spreading continues in the triangle between the tragal pointer, the mastoid and the posterior belly of digastric. The facial nerve trunk lies about one centimetre deep, and anterior and inferior to the pointer, at the depth of the digastric, six to eight millimetres deep to the tympanomastoid suture, and lateral to the styloid process. A nerve stimulator confirms it before anything over it is divided.

title: Pes anserinus and divisions
text: The trunk is followed forwards to the pes anserinus, where it divides. A fine haemostat is tunnelled along each division, and the gland tissue over it is divided, lifting the superficial gland off the nerve.

title: Lower division and the retromandibular vein
text: In the lower gland, the lower division and the marginal mandibular branch cross superficial to the retromandibular vein. The nerve is kept in view, and the vein or its branches are ligated if they bleed.

title: Branches to the anterior border
text: The temporal, zygomatic and buccal branches are followed to the anterior border of the gland, and the parotid duct is ligated. The superficial gland is removed with the tumour and a cuff of normal tissue, without breaching the capsule of a pleomorphic adenoma.

title: Check and close
text: The trunk is stimulated to confirm that every branch works. Haemostasis is checked and a drain is placed. A plication of the superficial musculo aponeurotic system, or a fat or fascial graft, can reduce Frey syndrome and the contour defect, and the wound is closed in layers.

title: Structures at risk
text: To summarise, the structures at risk are the facial nerve trunk, its temporal, zygomatic, buccal and marginal mandibular branches, the great auricular nerve, and the retromandibular vein. This film is for education only. Always check surgical detail against current atlases and senior guidance.
